title: Hilary Duff ate New England clam chowder and a Dunkin’ Munchkin on stage during her Mass. concert
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Hilary Duff sampled New England clam chowder and Dunkin' Munchkins on stage during her concert in Mansfield, Massachusetts.
Duff expressed trepidation but ultimately enjoyed the chowder's broth and potatoes, while remaining hesitant about clams.
The singer engaged with her audience by embracing local traditions and foods during her "The Lucky Me Tour" performances.

title: Adley Rutschman ready to make his debut with Red Sox on Tuesday
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman will debut for the Boston Red Sox against the Toronto Blue Jays on Tuesday.
Rutschman joined the Red Sox from the Orioles in a trade on August 3, following a wrist injury.
The Red Sox may not immediately use Rutschman in a regular role as he returns to full strength.

title: Springfield zoo suffers devastating damage during severe storm
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: The Zoo in Forest Park in Springfield remains closed after severe storm damage, including uprooted trees and destroyed enclosures.
No injuries were reported among the zoo's 200 animals, but the financial impact of the closure is significant.
A state of emergency was declared in Springfield due to power outages and damage, including a building collapse displacing 45 people.

title: 2 dead in crash on Marlborough highway
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Two people died in a multi-car crash on I-290 East in Marlborough, Massachusetts, Monday afternoon.
Massachusetts State Police, Marlborough Fire, and EMS responded to the crash before 3 p.m.
The Solomon Pond Road exit on I-290 East was closed, causing traffic delays and advising alternate routes.

title: Body recovered from Lake Quinsigamond in Shrewsbury
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Shrewsbury police received a report of a possible drowning at Lake Quinsigamond on Sunday afternoon.
A male body was found Monday morning near Sunset Beach after search efforts by local police and divers.
The drowning victim's identity is undisclosed, and the investigation by police is ongoing as of Monday evening.

title: Undrafted Patriots linebacker is carving out a roster spot
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Khalil Jacobs, undrafted from the University of Missouri, is impressing at the New England Patriots training camp.
Despite a 4.77 40-yard dash, Jacobs demonstrates game speed and versatility, impressing coaches including Mike Vrabel.
Jacobs competes for a role in the thin Patriots linebacker corps, standing out in intra-squad scrimmages.

title: Gov. Healey signed a law expanding abortion rights — here’s what to know
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Governor Maura Healey signed legislation removing gestational limits on abortion in Massachusetts, allowing greater physician discretion.
Massachusetts is now one of ten states with no statutory gestational limits, expanding abortion access past 24 weeks.
The legislation was opposed by the Massachusetts Family Institute, citing concerns over reduced oversight and protections for unborn children.

title: Lost gravestone of free Black man who died in 1729 uncovered in downtown Boston
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A gravestone of a free Black man, Sebastian, was found at Granary Burying Ground in Boston.
This gravestone, believed to be the oldest for a free Black person in the US, was restored and re-installed.
Sebastian, also known as Boston, advocated for marriage rights and had six children with his enslaved wife.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 13 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Carlton Davis and Will Campbell returned to practice; Campbell fully participated, while Davis was limited.
Romeo Doubs caught a touchdown in practice, showcasing his skills alongside Kyle Williams, who's competing for a receiver spot.
The Patriots will conduct a joint practice with the Colts before their preseason opener at Gillette Stadium.

title: Lifeguard dragged underwater by white shark at Maine beach
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A lifeguard in Scarborough, Maine, was briefly dragged underwater by a white shark while using a rescue torpedo.
The beach was closed for an hour after the incident for safety assessments and water monitoring by local officials.
Authorities warned of increased shark activity in the area and advised beachgoers to exercise caution and follow safety guidelines.
